recent_posts.title: Python Software Foundation News: PyCon US 2026: Why we're asking you to think about your hotel reservation
recent_posts.summary: PyCon US 2026 is facing a financial crisis due to significantly lower hotel block bookings compared to previous years. The PSF relies on hotel commissions to subsidize convention center costs and keep ticket prices affordable. As of mid-April 2026, only 2,192 hotel nights have been sold versus the 3,338 needed by April 20th to avoid paying over $200,000 in damages to hotels. The shortfall is attributed largely to declining international attendance due to the current geopolitical climate in the US. Attendees are urged to book official conference hotels through their PyCon US dashboard before the April 20th–24th deadlines.

recent_posts.title: Python Software Foundation News: Reflecting on Five Years as the PSF’s First CPython Developer in Residence
recent_posts.summary: Łukasz Langa, the inaugural CPython Developer in Residence at the Python Software Foundation, is stepping down after nearly five years. During his tenure he contributed to major CPython milestones including the migration to GitHub Issues, automating the CLA process, introducing free threading, and replacing the interactive shell. The Developer in Residence program has grown from one to five full-time engineers. Łukasz is joining Meta's Python Language Foundation team and moving to Vancouver, while remaining active in the open-source Python community. Meta will continue sponsoring the role at least through mid-2027.

recent_posts.title: Python Software Foundation News: Applications to Join the PSF Meetup Pro Network Are Back Open
recent_posts.summary: The Python Software Foundation (PSF) has reopened applications for Python Meetup groups to join its Meetup Pro Network, after a temporary suspension tied to the broader PSF Grants Program pause last August. Groups accepted into the network no longer pay Meetup subscription fees, with the PSF covering $15/month per group. Currently 109 groups are part of the network. To qualify, a Meetup group must offer majority Python content, include a Code of Conduct, and hold at least 2 events per year. The rest of the PSF Grants Program remains on hold while the foundation works on budgeting and long-term sustainability planning.

recent_posts.title: Python Software Foundation News: Join the Python Security Response Team!
recent_posts.summary: The Python Security Response Team (PSRT) has established formal governance through PEP 811, including public member lists, defined responsibilities, and a structured onboarding process. Jacob Coffee recently became the first new non-Release Manager member since 2023. The team published 16 vulnerability advisories in the past year and is seeking new members with security expertise to help coordinate vulnerability reports and remediations for CPython and pip.

recent_posts.title: Python Software Foundation News: Python is for Everyone: Inside the PSF's D&I Work Group
recent_posts.summary: The Python Software Foundation's Diversity & Inclusion Work Group was restructured in 2024 to ensure global representation across seven regions, with 19 active members working on three focused initiatives: creating D&I resources for communities, developing guides for starting local Python groups, and collecting community feedback through surveys. The group holds bimonthly meetings and annual panel discussions at PyCon US, addressing barriers like language-only announcements, inaccessible documentation, and lack of regional representation in Python leadership.

recent_posts.title: Python Software Foundation News: Introducing the PSF Community Partner Program
recent_posts.summary: The Python Software Foundation launched the Community Partner Program to provide non-financial support to Python events and initiatives through logo usage, name association, and social media promotion. The program emerged during the Grants Program pause as a way to continue supporting the community, offering an official "stamp of approval" that helps events attract sponsors. Applications require a one-page form, enforceable Code of Conduct, and six weeks advance notice, with review by the Grants Work Group.

recent_posts.title: Python Software Foundation News: Your Python. Your Voice. Join the Python Developers Survey 2026!
recent_posts.summary: The ninth annual Python Developers Survey is now open, launching in January 2026 to enable same-year results publication. The 10-15 minute survey captures the current state of Python and its ecosystem, with translations available in eight languages including Chinese, Japanese, and Spanish. A promotion kit with multilingual social media posts is available to help spread awareness. The survey is a partnership between the Python Software Foundation and JetBrains, with 20 participants randomly selected to receive $100 gift cards.

recent_posts.title: Python Software Foundation News: Departing the Python Software Foundation (Staff)
recent_posts.summary: Ee Durbin announces their departure as Director of Infrastructure at the Python Software Foundation after years of managing Python's technical infrastructure and PyPI. They will continue supporting the PSF part-time for six months during the transition and plan to remain active as a community volunteer. The PSF has built a team to distribute the responsibilities previously held by Durbin.

recent_posts.title: Python Software Foundation News: Anthropic invests $1.5 million in the Python Software Foundation and open source security
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic has committed $1.5 million over two years to the Python Software Foundation, focusing on ecosystem security improvements. The funding will support automated proactive malware detection for PyPI packages, creation of a malware dataset for capability analysis, and development of security tools potentially transferable to other open source repositories. Additional funds will sustain core PSF operations including CPython development, community grants, and infrastructure maintenance.

recent_posts.title: Python Software Foundation News: Sovereign Tech Agency and PSF Security Partnership
recent_posts.summary: The Sovereign Tech Agency is investing €86,000 in Python Software Foundation security initiatives. The funding will support two key projects: developing fuzz-testing infrastructure for CPython's tarfile and zipfile modules to prevent archive-handling vulnerabilities, and implementing OAuth 2.0/OIDC-based account recovery for PyPI to improve account integrity while reducing support burden. Both initiatives aim to strengthen critical components of the Python software supply chain.
